script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

A cozy living room. A fire burns in the hearth. Snow falls gently outside the window. We hear the sound of rain tapping on the roof.

FRANK (50s, rugged, kind) sits in a worn-out armchair. He stares into the fire, lost in thought. His wife, MARY (50s, caring, warm), enters the room. She wears a dressing gown and carries a steaming mug of tea.

MARY
(softly)
Frank, are you all right?

FRANK
(sighs)
I've been thinking about our past, Mary. About all the things I could have done differently.

MARY
(sits down next to him)
We all have regrets, Frank. But we can't change the past. What we can do is make the most of the present and look forward to the future.

Frank nods, taking a sip of his tea.

INT. KITCHEN - DAY

Mary cooks breakfast for their adult children, JESS (20s, rebellious, angry) and SAM (20s, sensitive, introspective). Frank enters the kitchen, wearing a freshly pressed shirt.

FRANK
(smiling)
Good morning, sleepyheads.

JESS
(scoffs)
Morning, Dad.

SAM
(smiling back at Frank)
Morning, Dad.

INT. DINING ROOM - DAY

The family sits down to eat breakfast. The mood is tense.

JESS
(angrily)
I can't believe you're still working that dead-end job, Dad.

FRANK
(calmly)
It pays the bills, Jess. And it gives me the chance to provide for you and Sam.

MARY
(gently)
Jess, please. Your father is doing the best he can.

Jess rolls her eyes, obviously unimpressed.

INT. FRANK'S OFFICE - DAY

Frank sits at his desk, staring at a stack of unopened mail. He looks out the window and sees a young boy, MIKEY (8), playing alone in the snow.

FRANK
(to himself)
I should go talk to him.

INT. PARK - DAY

Frank approaches Mikey, who is building a snowman.

MIKEY
(looking up, surprised)
Hey, mister.

FRANK
(smiling)
Hi there, Mikey. Mind if I help you build a snowman?

Mikey shakes his head and they work together, chatting amicably.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

The family gathers around the fire. Mary plays a piano in the background.

FRANK
(looking at Jess and Sam)
You know, I used to play the piano when I was young. Maybe I should start again.

SAM
(excitedly)
Yes, Dad! I can help you find a teacher.

JESS
(rolling her eyes)
Great, another hobby.

MARY
(gently)
Jess, be nice. Your father is trying to make the most of his life.

INT. FRANK'S PIANO ROOM - DAY

Frank and Sam sit side by side at the piano. Frank struggles to read the music, but Sam encourages him.

FRANK
(laughing)
I don't think I'll ever be as good as I used to be.

SAM
(smiling)
It's not about being good, Dad. It's about enjoying the journey.

INT. KITCHEN - NIGHT

Mary, Frank, Jess, and Sam sit around the kitchen table, eating dinner. The mood is much more relaxed and positive.

FRANK
(looking around the table)
I'm glad we're all here, together.

MARY
(smiling)
Me too, Frank.

JESS
(looking at her father)
Dad, I'm sorry for the way I've been acting.

FRANK
(smiling back)
Apology accepted, Jess.

SAM
(turning to his father)
Dad, I want to thank you for always being there for us, no matter what.

Frank smiles, tears welling up in his eyes.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

The family sits around the fire, enjoying each other's company. Frank looks at his wife and children, feeling a sense of pride and gratitude.

FRANK
(whispering to Mary)
You were right. We can't change the past, but we can make the most of the present and look forward to the future.

MARY
(smiling)
I'm glad you see that now, Frank.

They hold hands as the fire crackles and the snow falls gently outside.

FADE OUT.
